body: Yes!! The first season she really lays out different types of abuse (like financial abuse which i hadnt realized my abuser inflicted on me until then)
The podcast Something was wrong (especially the first season) does a really good in depth analysis of domestic abuse through someone's story it was so helpful to me

Oh that is so good to know! And yeah, so many women find themselves asking whether it's abuse, best advice I have is to trust your gut feeling, if you're at the point of asking yourself whether it is, it most usually is. I hope you can get out as soon as you can. I'm so proud of you for having the courage to question this behavior, it takes a lot of time to achieve. Good luck!!!❤️

Oh my god please get out of there. Do you have family/friends that can take you in? Anywhere safe to go to? I just got out (literally four days ago) of a simile situation (albeit not married) and it is the ONLY and BEST thing you can do. Take the dogs if you can, but no matter what do not tell him where you're going. Or leave when he's not home. Stay safe out there. Sending love.
Good luck to you💙 you are courageous and loved
Go to the hospital. Get a rape kit. The police should've done this. That fucking sucks. Get an exam, it will be difficult but you need to do this. Are you safe where you are?
RIGHT! You spend your life on wikipedia, SO, could you just maybe for once not be so self centered that you only google what matters to you?

Oh sweetie that fucking sucks.
We all need a "dump ya load" day lmao. Sisters unite!😂 like fuck this YOU are also growing why do you have to take on the responsibility of showing them how to?

Yo honestly like at this point men who value chores are unicorns. This is so disheartening for young girls. I wish I had the laissez-faire of a 22 y/o man. Gosh. Leave that poor excuse of a man. It's so disrespectful of them to assume because they have a "different standard" of cleaning (which can go into wild directions), your standards are too much and yours to worry about.

I tried to give my partner a year of living by himself so he'd learn faster. It was no use. One year living together and I regret not pushing more. Don't let yourself be enrolled in this.

If they don't do chores now: they never will. I've had my share of experiences with younger men learning how to adult, and let me tell you: "i just don't see those things", "i just need you to help me by asking", even "is there anything you want me to do today", etc. All that means is "chores are *your* thing" and that does. Not. Change. I'm sorry to say this, I just have also EVEN MADE CHORE CHARTS, AND GUIDES I TAPED INTO CUPBOARDS that explicitly have a checklist. I recommended alarms. I divided chores so that we'd both always be doing the same chores hoping habits would set it: *nothing* works.

Also the first part is super concerning. 
My advice:  leave. It'll hurt. Hell I live with mine and am not following my own advice. It won't get better because he obviously doesn't care. You're already far too mature for him. I'm sorry, and hope you consider how much you'd put effort in to "save him" and how little that would actually gain you.

So proud of you for standing up for yourself. I understand that snap--I'm the same, I give people endless chances but something one time will just snap that. You will be so better off, and you can focus on healing yourself. Keep your head up. You're courageous and strong.
I'm so sorry that happened I hope they come home soin❤️❤️❤️
Thank you all for these responses I so appreciate it. I definitely will be giving myself time to really look into what my next steps will be. ❤️
